clue.text: Limit, quite precise, set by engineers

indicators.note: set by places one piece beside the other, here the engineers first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army
strict means exact, quite precise

explanation.surface: A boundary marked out to an exacting standard by a team of engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict something is to confine it within bounds, a synonym of limit as a verb.

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A musical note is offered as an incorrect answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or witty reply, an answer.

clue.text: Take a youngster on board for some food

indicators.note: take, with on board, means to absorb, so the ship letters hold the youngster

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so being on board means being on a ship
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: Bringing a child aboard in exchange for some provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ... on board' places A LAD inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are dishes of raw vegetables, a type of food.

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, so not for the first time
to con a text is to study it, to read it

explanation.surface: Someone has been tricked yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conned' looks like swindled, but in its old sense it means studied or read.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying a text once more is going over it again, which is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Good sense shown by Conservative leader on discipline

indicators.note: leader on puts the party word at the front, ahead of the discipline

parts.note: a science is a discipline or branch of knowledge

explanation.surface: A Tory chief shows sound judgement on matters of school discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscience is the moral faculty telling right from wrong, a sense of what is good.

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword stand-in for many
asses are donkeys, a kind of animal

explanation.surface: Someone rounds up a large herd of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To mass people or things is to gather them into one body, so the verb fits bringing together.

clue.text: The heights to which one may rise!

definitions.text: The heights to which one may rise!

parts.words: The heights to which one may rise!
parts.note: reads like a motto about ambition and success, but literally means the elevation a climber or aircraft reaches

explanation.definitionFit: Altitude is height above sea level, the elevation reached when ascending.

indicators.note: all bad suggests everything gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dried fruit and nuts, sadly, have all gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultanas are dried seedless grapes, a kind of fruit.

parts.note: yarn is thread or string

indicators.note: upturn in a down clue means the word for about is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A tale about an economic recovery and a ray of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a story but is thread; 'upturn' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringer is a long horizontal timber or girder in a structure, a beam.

clue.text: A lot rent accommodation for freedom

indicators.note: accommodation suggests making room and arranging, so these words are rearranged to fit together

explanation.surface: A lot of rent paid for lodgings buys a sense of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' signals the rearrangement of the letters of A LOT RENT; 'for freedom' is the definition, describing someone in favour of letting others act freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A permissive person allows others liberty, so being in favour of freedom describes that attitude.

parts.note: the head of skin is its first letter
a relation is a story or account, a tale

explanation.surface: A question about whether flattering a shaven-headed relative is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a verb meaning praise, but it is the comparative of flat, as beer goes flat; 'skinhead' gives the first letter of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale bread or beer has lost its freshness or fizz, so more stale means more flat.

clue.text: Got upset and cried, so clearing out

indicators.note: got upset suggests being knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone became distressed and wept while emptying a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is the act of getting rid of something unwanted, a removal or clearance.
A strain is a tune or melody, as an air is; strain also means exert or push hard, as force does.

parts.note: to journey is to travel
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Going on a trip together with a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman who works for an employer, a skilled worker.

indicators.note: after places the judge piece following the support piece

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A fair verdict delivered by a judge once backing has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' here means mediocre, as in fair to middling, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of only middling quality matches something inferior or mediocre.

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
the Tories, Britain's Conservatives, are the political right

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims a curse against the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, say, but is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and outright both mean complete or total, as in an outright lie.

clue.text: Stand up for the person taking the case

explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to support publicly; an advocate is also a lawyer who argues a client's cause in court.

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the leftist word holds the others word inside

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A left-winger is held back by other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested means halted or checked, as growth can be arrested, so it means stopped.

parts.note: not yet reaching a figure is being under it
a score is twenty

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that a person has not yet reached twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to highlight it, as a line drawn beneath words does.

clue.text: Having to sing out for a drink

indicators.note: out suggests being wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being required to sing in order to earn a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: STINGO is an old word for strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is a strong old English beer, a drink.

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a
to fancy something is to like it

explanation.surface: A fancy French piece described as beyond comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that cannot be compared are dissimilar, quite different from each other.

clue.text: Thin, but that's of little consequence

explanation.definitionFit: Slight describes a slender, slim build and also something trivial or unimportant.

indicators.note: with sound tells us the word for ways is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: roads are ways or routes

explanation.surface: An island noted for its well-made, solid routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but here it signals that ROADS is heard, giving the Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, home of the ancient Colossus.

clue.text: The guard's quarters reorganised in Lent

parts.note: quarters are compass points; S and E (south and east) are two of them

indicators.note: reorganised says these letters are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A guard's living quarters have been rearranged during the Lenten season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings but supplies S and E, two compass quarters, which are shuffled with IN LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier posted to keep watch, a guard.

parts.note: ants are social insects, and worker ants form most of a colony

explanation.surface: Greek welfare staff are said to be making allowances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social workers' looks like care staff but means ants, insects that live in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Grants are sums of money given for a purpose, which are allowances.

explanation.surface: Altering the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister but means post meridiem: the afternoon comes when AM is ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Amending is altering or revising; read as A.M. ending, it describes the afternoon, which begins when morning finishes.

clue.text: Strive without end to be up-to the-minute

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the strive word goes round the other

parts.note: to try is to strive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Endless effort is needed to stay fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' reads as endless, but 'without' means outside, so TRY wraps round END.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable and current, as up-to-the-minute does.

indicators.note: ill-written suggests letters set down badly, so these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Cheeky verses that are not badly composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy means cheeky and impudent, as a rude, disrespectful manner is.
